security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives from Markdown fences, inline command examples, placeholder configuration values, reference links, and multilingual text. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, dynamic execution, or hidden binary content in SKILL.md. The skill declares Bash and includes read-only project inspection examples, so command use should remain explicit and user-approved.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger command and secret scanners.
remediation.suggestion: State that shell snippets are examples and should run only after user approval.

remediation.issue: The skill declares Bash for a documentation workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Limit Bash usage to read-only inspection commands, or remove Bash when repository context is supplied.
Add guidance to never print or copy populated secret files into README content.

content.value_statement: New contributors often lose time finding setup steps, architecture context, and ownership rules. This skill turns project facts into a structured README that supports onboarding, debugging, and delivery.
actual_capabilities: Defines an eleven-section README structure for developer onboarding.
Covers system overview, repo map, local setup, configuration, data model, CI, debugging, security, and working agreements.
Provides checklist questions to verify a README supports new engineers.
Includes sample Markdown layouts for common README sections.
Suggests project inspection commands for folder structure, package metadata, and environment examples.
limitations: Does not discover repository details without reading the target project.
Does not replace architecture diagrams, runbooks, or API documentation.
Shell examples are generic and may need project-specific adjustment.
Requires human review for secrets guidance and production deployment details.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Engineers
use_cases.description: Create a fast path that explains setup, architecture, core flows, debugging, and team agreements.

use_cases.title: Document Existing Repositories
use_cases.description: Turn scattered project knowledge into a README that links to deeper docs without duplicating everything.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Handoffs
use_cases.description: Prepare a consistent developer handoff document before ownership changes, audits, or team transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Starter README
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new repository README.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a developer README for this repository. Include fast path, local setup, repo map, and working agreement.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing README
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a README that already exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current README for developer onboarding gaps. Update it with missing setup, architecture, configuration, and debugging sections.

prompt_templates.title: Add Release And Debugging Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for operational onboarding details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Expand the README with CI, release, rollback, observability, common failures, and ownership guidance for new maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Build Full Handoff README
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before a team handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete developer handoff README. Cover goals, non-goals, core flows, data model, security, docs index, and open decisions.

output_examples.input: A repository has setup notes, but no onboarding path for new engineers.
output: A README starts with a 30-minute fast path.
It links setup, system overview, core flows, debugging, and first-task guidance.
It separates deep reference material into dedicated docs.

output_examples.input: A team wants a better README before transferring ownership.
output: The README describes goals, non-goals, data ownership, release rules, and rollback steps.
It identifies key entry points and common failure points.
It lists follow-up docs that must stay current.

output_examples.input: A README contains marketing copy but little engineering context.
output: The revised document removes vague claims and adds setup, architecture, commands, and team practices.
Each section answers a practical question for a new developer.

best_practices: Keep the README as a map and link detailed reference docs.
Verify every setup command with a clean local environment.
Document secrets by variable purpose, never by real secret value.
anti_patterns: Do not replace onboarding guidance with marketing claims.
Do not list folders without explaining ownership and purpose.
Do not paste secret values or production credentials into examples.

faq.question: What type of README does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates developer onboarding READMEs focused on setup, architecture, workflows, debugging, and working agreements.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify missing developer sections and rewrite the README around practical onboarding needs.

faq.question: Does it generate project facts automatically?
faq.answer: It needs repository context from files, commands, or user notes before it can describe project-specific details.

faq.question: Is it only for web projects?
faq.answer: No. The structure works for most software projects, but examples may need adjustment for each stack.

faq.question: How should teams handle secrets in the README?
faq.answer: Document variable names, purpose, and storage location. Do not include real credentials or private connection strings.
